sources.title: Media Distillery: products and delivery model
From Linear Broadcast to Topic-Based Viewing
Media Distillery and Gracenote integrate EPG correction

items.title: Delivery economics begin with accepted output
items.summary: Source observation: Media Distillery describes managed API delivery and subscriptions based on streams, content volume or generated outputs.
items.implication: Model inference: Model accepted downstream consumption, billable-unit reconciliation and a pilot baseline before expanding coverage.

items.title: Replay requires the real programme timeline
items.summary: Source observation: The Time Marker Suite includes programme boundary correction and episode navigation markers.
items.implication: Model inference: Treat schedule time as an input hypothesis; certify true boundaries and preserve ordinary playback when confidence is insufficient.

items.title: Ad detection has to work beyond known signals
items.summary: Source observation: The Swisscom case describes deployment on 50 channels, including channels lacking ad-break signalling, after difficulties generalizing an internal detector.
items.implication: Model inference: Adopt a channel-specific adjudication set and separate break detection from the operator’s entitlement and ad decisions.

items.title: Discovery includes more than catalogue text
items.summary: Source observation: The Search & Discovery Suite lists previews, short-form output, chapters, episodic images and semantic search.
items.implication: Model inference: Use one programme identity and provenance model across these outputs so improvements reach actual browsing and playback surfaces.

items.title: Chaptering can expose value inside long programmes
items.summary: Source observation: The NLZIET case reports around 400 hours enriched monthly and chapter delivery about 15 minutes after broadcast in its case context.
items.implication: Model inference: Set freshness and language acceptance by genre and operator; avoid treating a case-study latency as a universal SLA.

items.title: Event-cohort engagement needs careful interpretation
items.summary: Source observation: For the 2026 Winter Olympics, the NLZIET case reports 15% of on-demand viewers using chapters and five-times engagement compared with regular programming.
items.implication: Model inference: Evaluate event cohorts separately: audience intent and tournament conditions differ, so this comparison does not establish causal lift or a reusable forecast.

items.title: Previews need a production editorial workflow
items.summary: Source observation: Sunrise’s case describes TV Highlights powered by Preview Distillery for content selection.
items.implication: Model inference: Review spoiler risk, episode alignment and time spent correcting output alongside viewer conversion.

items.title: Sports context extends beyond the match
items.summary: Source observation: The Sports Engagement Suite includes match highlights, navigation, sports chapters and related shoulder content.
items.implication: Model inference: Keep event identity, replay chronology and output rights consistent across live moments and related interviews.

items.title: Content context is a separate monetization signal
items.summary: Source observation: The Time Marker Suite offers content-context advertising tags alongside ad-break markers.
items.implication: Model inference: Keep suitability judgments and ad decisions separate; contextual metadata should not require building viewer identity profiles.

items.title: Metadata partnerships are part of the delivery path
items.summary: Source observation: Gracenote documents an EPG correction partnership and its Schedules API identifies Media Distillery as a possible exact-timing source for entitled clients.
items.implication: Model inference: Certify mapping, entitlement and precedence through the partner route; model Gracenote as partner/adjacent provider in the landscape.

items.title: The investment reference is historical context
items.summary: Source observation: Vortex records investment alongside Peak Capital in June 2016 and lists Media Distillery as a current investment at access.
items.implication: Model inference: Use 2016 for Vortex package placement. Do not infer valuation, funding runway, ownership proportions or a buy-and-build roadmap.

items.title: Specialist operation is part of the value proposition
items.summary: Source observation: Media Distillery describes a team of AI engineers, developers and video experts supporting video services.
items.implication: Model inference: Model accountable product and operational teams while clearly labeling staffing and ownership as a proposed design; public biographies are not an org chart.
